description: contracts/sprint-2.md's own 'Deferred-obligation disposition' section lists PROP-303e among the '26 orchestrator-blocked Tier>0' obligations in its '31 targeted for closure this sprint' bucket. But the SAME contract's own 'Files touched' section explicitly admits: 'The ... lease-shell/job-ssh secrets-injection helper (REQ-303's own FIND-403/FIND-401 corrections) were NOT created this sprint -- both belong exclusively to PROP-303b's own real Akash deploy path, which the "Deferred-obligation disposition" section below explicitly re-defers as Tier-3'. PROP-303e's own verification-architecture.md row (line ~697) names EXACTLY this artifact as its verification target: 'After deploy-akash.sh's manifest-send succeeds, a NEW provider-services lease-shell <service> "cat > /opt/anicca.env" --stdin step (this feature's own orchestration code, never a deploy-akash.sh modification) delivers the child's pre-generated wallet material onto the leased container' -- i.e. PROP-303e IS the lease-shell secrets-injection helper the contract's own 'Files touched' section admits was never built. An independent grep across the ENTIRE ~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/ tree (source AND tests) for 'lease-shell'/'PROP-303e' finds ZERO matches of any kind -- not even a stub, a skipped test, or a deps-injection seam a future test could target. This is the IDENTICAL root-cause pattern round-2's own FIND-005 already established and fixed for PROP-203c/PROP-303f ('both join PROP-303b's own Tier-3 deferral, since building a custom SDL variant for a deploy that itself will not run this sprint is equally premature') -- PROP-303e is the EXACT SAME category of obligation (an artifact that exists ONLY inside PROP-303b's own real-deploy path, which this sprint's own contract already Tier-3-defers) but was never moved into the 'genuinely require infrastructure this sprint does not build' re-deferred bucket alongside its siblings, an apparent editorial oversight in the contract's own reconciliation. Under CRIT-205's own passThreshold ('FAIL if any of the 31 names a call site that does not exist in the current implementation, is unreachable, or is a stub/placeholder'), PROP-303e is an unambiguous FAIL: its named call site does not exist anywhere in the current implementation, in any form, and the contract's own text independently corroborates this absence is intentional (deferred, not merely unbuilt-by-oversight) -- yet PROP-303e itself remains mis-scoped into the 'targeted for closure this sprint' bucket rather than the 'additionally re-deferred' one, which is itself a spec-fidelity defect in contracts/sprint-2.md distinct from any implementation gap.
